items.q: Which antibody is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
items.exp: Anti Smith is highly specific for lupus though insensitive. Antinuclear antibody is the sensitive screening test but occurs in many conditions and healthy people.
r: Incorrect. ANA is sensitive but not specific.
Correct. Anti Smith is the most specific lupus antibody here.
Incorrect. Rheumatoid factor supports rheumatoid arthritis non-specifically.
Incorrect. Anticentromere points to limited systemic sclerosis.
items.kp: Specific for lupus: anti Smith and anti dsDNA; sensitive: ANA.

items.q: Falling complement with rising anti double stranded DNA in lupus most suggests what?
items.exp: Active lupus consumes complement through immune complexes while anti dsDNA rises, a pattern that tracks flares and nephritis. Monitoring both together guides treatment intensity.
r: Incorrect. Quiescent disease usually normalises complement.
Correct. Consumption plus rising dsDNA signals active flare.
Incorrect. Resolution would reverse this pattern.
Incorrect. Deficiency is possible but flare is the stem intent.
items.kp: Low complement plus high dsDNA equals active lupus until proven otherwise.

items.q: Wire loop glomerular deposits in lupus nephritis are located where?
items.exp: Wire loop deposits are large subendothelial immune complexes thickening capillary walls in proliferative lupus nephritis. Subepithelial deposits characterise the membranous class instead.
r: Incorrect. Subepithelial deposits define membranous lupus.
Correct. Wire loops are subendothelial deposits.
Incorrect. Mesangial deposits occur in milder classes.
Incorrect. Tubular deposits do not form wire loops.
items.kp: Wire loop equals subendothelial equals proliferative lupus.

items.q: Dry eyes, dry mouth, parotid swelling and anti Ro antibodies define which syndrome?
items.exp: Sjogren syndrome is lymphocytic destruction of lacrimal and salivary glands with anti Ro and anti La antibodies. Long standing disease increases lymphoma risk.
r: Incorrect. Sclerosis causes skin fibrosis and Raynaud.
Correct. Sicca symptoms plus anti Ro mean Sjogren syndrome.
Incorrect. Dermatomyositis causes weakness and heliotrope rash.
Incorrect. Mixed disease centres on anti U1 RNP.
items.kp: Sicca plus anti Ro or La: think Sjogren.

items.q: CREST features with anticentromere antibody indicate which form of systemic sclerosis?
items.exp: Limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis produces CREST features and associates with anticentromere antibody and later pulmonary hypertension. Diffuse disease associates with anti Scl 70 and interstitial lung disease.
r: Incorrect. Diffuse disease links to anti Scl 70.
Correct. CREST plus anticentromere means limited disease.
Incorrect. Sine disease lacks skin change but is not defined by CREST.
Incorrect. Overlap does not define this antibody pattern.
items.kp: Centromere limited, Scl 70 diffuse: a durable exam pairing.

items.q: Drug induced lupus from hydralazine or procainamide most characteristically shows which antibody?
o: Anti double stranded DNA high titre
items.exp: Drug induced lupus associates with anti histone antibodies and usually spares kidney and brain, resolving after drug withdrawal. Classic triggers include procainamide, hydralazine and isoniazid.
r: Incorrect. Anti Smith marks idiopathic lupus.
Correct. Anti histone characterises drug induced lupus.
Incorrect. High dsDNA favours idiopathic active lupus.
Incorrect. Anti Ro favours Sjogren and neonatal lupus.
items.kp: Drug induced lupus: anti histone, milder course.

items.q: Failure of central tolerance from AIRE gene mutation causes which syndrome?
items.exp: AIRE enables thymic expression of self antigens for negative selection. Its failure causes autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1 with candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism and adrenal failure.
r: Incorrect. DiGeorge is thymic hypoplasia with T cell deficiency.
Correct. AIRE failure breaks central tolerance.
Incorrect. Bruton disease blocks B cell development.
Incorrect. Granulomatous disease is a phagocyte burst defect.
items.kp: AIRE teaches the thymus self; its loss causes multiorgan autoimmunity.

items.q: Rheumatoid arthritis most specifically associates with which antibody?
items.exp: Anti cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies are highly specific for rheumatoid arthritis and predict erosive disease. Rheumatoid factor is sensitive but far less specific.
r: Correct. Anti CCP is the specific rheumatoid marker.
Incorrect. ANA alone is too non-specific.
Incorrect. Anti mitochondrial marks primary biliary cholangitis.
Incorrect. Anti GBM marks Goodpasture syndrome.
items.kp: For rheumatoid specificity choose anti CCP over rheumatoid factor.

items.q: Anti U1 ribonucleoprotein antibody with overlapping lupus, sclerosis and myositis features defines what?
items.exp: Mixed connective tissue disease combines features of lupus, systemic sclerosis and myositis with high titre anti U1 RNP. Raynaud phenomenon and swollen hands are early clues.
r: Incorrect. Sjogren centres on sicca and anti Ro.
Correct. Overlap plus anti U1 RNP means mixed connective tissue disease.
Incorrect. Antiphospholipid disease causes clots and pregnancy loss.
Incorrect. Polyarteritis is a necrotising vasculitis.
items.kp: Overlap features plus U1 RNP equals mixed connective tissue disease.

items.q: Antiphospholipid syndrome is defined clinically by which pairing?
items.exp: Antiphospholipid syndrome causes arterial and venous thrombosis with recurrent fetal loss from placental thrombosis, associated with lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin and anti beta2 glycoprotein antibodies.
r: Incorrect. Haemolysis suggests a different haematological process.
Correct. Clots plus pregnancy loss define the syndrome.
Incorrect. Gut symptoms do not define it.
Incorrect. Haemoptysis with sinusitis suggests small vessel vasculitis.
items.kp: Clot plus miscarriage: test for antiphospholipid antibodies.
